description: Pest control, K9 bed bug detection & rodent control in Montmorenci, Aiken SC. Family-owned, safe for kids & pets, same-week service. Call 803-226-3155.
h1: Pest Control in Montmorenci, SC

hero.lead: Montmorenci is an unincorporated community in Aiken County, on U.S. Route 78 about five miles southeast of Aiken. No town limits, no municipal code office, no city inspector. Coastal K-9 & Pest Solutions covers household pests, rodent exclusion and trapping, cockroaches and K-9 bed bug screening out here, where the repair has to stand on its own.
hero.meta: Call 803-226-3155 · ZIP 29839, along the U.S. 78 corridor · Kim@ck9ps.com · Coastal K-9 & Pest Solutions, 320 Wendy Lane, Windsor, SC 29856

body:
Most pest control writing assumes the place it describes has a government — that somebody could be called about the derelict structure across the road, and that the water at your tap is a utility’s problem.

Neither assumption survives here. Montmorenci is a named community in unincorporated Aiken County, not a chartered town, and that changes the shape of the work.

1,070.7Square miles of Aiken County against 21.8 for the City of Aiken, most of it under no municipal government (Census Reporter)
1,132Farms in Aiken County across 138,479 acres (2022 Census of Agriculture). A COUNTY figure, not a Montmorenci one
44 inSand above the clay in the Troup soil series typical here, rapidly permeable up top (USDA soil series description)

What does it actually mean that Montmorenci is not a town?

It means nothing sits between you and Aiken County. Montmorenci is an unincorporated community, not a town and not a census-designated place. It stands at 482 feet on U.S. 78, about 5.3 miles southeast of Aiken, in ZIP 29839, with a post office.

The Census Bureau does not enumerate it as a place, so no population figure exists for it. Anyone quoting one has borrowed it from a ZIP code or a tract. Where context is needed below we use county numbers and label them county.

A railroad station and turning facility went in here in 1833, making this a shipping point for cotton bound for Augusta. It grew as a stop serving a plantation district and never incorporated.

Who enforces anything about the property next door?

Not a city, because there is not one. No municipal code office, no town ordinance reaching the parcel across the fence line, no inspector who will drive out and look.

Rodents ignore property lines. A house mouse feeds within roughly ten to thirty feet of its nest, so a mouse problem is genuinely yours. A Norway rat ranges commonly a hundred feet or more from the burrow, which puts a collapsed feed shed on the adjoining tract inside the population pressing on your house.

We are a pest control company, not a law office, and this page offers no legal advice. Aiken County is the unit of local government here, and what it regulates is the county’s answer to give. The practical consequence is ours: when the reservoir next door will not change, the strategy moves onto your own ground.

What does the general program cover at an address like this?

The same four things we sell everywhere, applied to a property that is its own small utility district. General pest control here leans on the exterior.

  • Scheduled service on a treated perimeter, plus eaves, soffits and thresholds
  • Ant identification first — fire, odorous house and carpenter ants are three separate jobs
  • Cockroach control, split between the drain-and-septic problem and the carried-in problem
  • K-9 rodent detection with rat and mouse trapping rather than a bait-first program
  • Canine screening and bed bug treatment
  • Sealing and exclusion carpentry, so an opening is measured and closed once

No termite work, no wood infestation reports, no mosquito or turf program. Saying so now is cheaper than learning it later.

Which parts of the property count as pest infrastructure?

On a serviced street, water and waste belong to a utility. Here they are four structures on your own land.

The well head and its cap

A modern well finishes in a vented sanitary cap, and that vent is screened for a reason. Caps crack, screens corrode, and a casing bumped by a mower sits proud of its gasket. The resulting gap is usually larger than a mouse requires.

The pump house

This failure rarely arrives as a pest call. Rodents chew the low-voltage run to the pressure switch, the symptom is no water, and the contractor who fixes it sees the nesting without mentioning it.

The tank lid, riser and cleanout

A septic tank is warm, wet and permanently stocked, which makes excellent American cockroach habitat. What keeps that population outdoors is a seated riser lid, an intact cleanout cap and water standing in every trap. A guest bathroom nobody runs loses its seal in weeks.

The drain field

Trench backfill is the softest, dampest ground on a sandy lot, so burrowing follows it. Anything ponding above a field is a failure signal and a moisture source, and moisture turns occasional invaders into a standing complaint.

Why does a well head change the product decision?

Because no treatment plant stands between a mistake and your kitchen tap. Soils here are deep sands — the Troup series runs sand from the surface to about 44 inches before clay begins, rapidly permeable up top. Aiken County averages 50.77 inches of rain a year, and on that profile water moves down rather than sideways.

So the rule near a well head is mechanical before chemical: seal the cap, clear stored material back from the casing, trap instead of bait. Pesticide labels carry restrictions concerning wells and water, those directions bind the licensed applicator, and a technician who cannot say where the label stops him is the wrong one for this property.

How do you seal a house when nobody is coming to inspect it?

With a tape measure, because the standard is dimensional and nobody out here will ever check it.

  • The pencil test: a pencil is close to a quarter inch across. Wherever it slides in, a house mouse follows.
  • Rats: allow no more than half an inch anywhere, and check the corners of barn and garage doors where seals harden.
  • Foundation and crawl vents: back them in woven hardware cloth. Welded and knitted mesh lets go at the joins.
  • Mesh spec: half-inch openings at 19 gauge for rats; quarter-inch at 24 gauge for mice. Thinner wire is decoration.
  • Utility penetrations: water line, conduit, hose bib and well line all pass through oversize holes. Cap rigidly, then pack behind it.
  • Dryer vent: fit a rodent-resistant hood with a working damper. Fine screen over a dryer duct starts lint fires.
  • Masonry: mortar or hydraulic cement, never sealant. Sheet metal at 24 gauge on door edges and sill corners.
  • Order of work: close the shell only once the inside is quiet, or you seal animals in with your floor system.

Our exclusion crew treats this as carpentry. The measurement is the enforcement.

Why is bait the wrong opening move on a property with animals?

Two reasons, and the second one decides it.

The first is the animals. Farm dogs, barn cats and poultry investigate what they find, and secondary exposure of predators and scavengers to anticoagulant rodenticides is documented in the literature. We have no South Carolina monitoring figure and will not invent one, but the mechanism is undisputed.

The second reason is structural: bait lowers a population, it never closes a door. On an unincorporated rural lot the outdoor supply is effectively unlimited — fields, stored feed, a woodline, the adjoining tract no ordinance reaches. Clear the animals inside and the same route refills within weeks, so a bait-led program never ends.

Rodenticide keeps a legitimate place: secured tamper-resistant exterior stations, mapped and serviced by a licensed applicator, never loose and never in a feed room. Under the EPA rodenticide risk mitigation decision, loose pellet products left the consumer market and consumer baits ship in preloaded stations. Our house mouse and Norway rat profiles cover what each one does.

German or American cockroach in a house on septic?

The distinction decides the treatment, and on a septic property one of the two lives on your land permanently.

The American cockroach is the large one, an inch and a half of reddish brown, living outdoors and below ground. Tanks, drain lines, cleanouts and mulch beds are normal habitat. Indoors it turns up singly, at night, near a drain, having used a route a seated lid or a refilled trap would have closed.

The German cockroach does not survive outside in this climate and never walks in from a field. It arrives inside an object: a secondhand appliance, delivery cardboard, gear returning from a camp or a rental. No landlord, no adjoining unit, no property manager — which means thorough work here genuinely finishes.

Identify on size and behavior. Half an inch, tan, twice striped behind the head and clustered near warmth is German. Large and solitary near a drain is American.

What does a canine bed bug screen settle out here?

Whether anything is present at all, which is what a flashlight answers worst early on. Distance from town protects nobody: bed bugs travel on people and possessions, not across ground.

Montmorenci carries a specific version of that exposure. Several early nineteenth century Greek Revival houses here still stand, and some antebellum homes now operate as inns with equine amenities. Lodging runs on guest turnover, and guest turnover is the transmission mechanism — so those buildings get handled as commercial accounts with monitoring.

A visual inspection means stripping beds and working seams and frame joints by hand. It is reliable once an infestation is heavy, unreliable before that, and a search finding nothing has proved nothing. A trained dog reads odor, clears a large old house including the guest room used twice a year, and narrows it to a spot we confirm by hand. Published field validation runs deepest for bed bugs specifically, which is why we attach no accuracy percentage to structural rodent work — reasoning set out on our canine scent detection accuracy page.

Which regulator actually reaches this address?

One does, and it is not local. Structural pest control in South Carolina is licensed by the Clemson University Department of Pesticide Regulation — a land-grant university function, not a state agriculture department, which defeats most people trying to verify a company. Structural work is Category 7A.

LayerInside a cityUnincorporated Aiken County
Code enforcementMunicipal officeNone municipal; the county is the local government
Building regulationCity inspection departmentAdministered at county level
Water and wasteUtility owned systemCommonly a private well and septic field
Pest control licensingClemson DPR, statewideClemson DPR, statewide — the same either way
Product use restrictionsFederal labelFederal label — the same either way

The firm must hold a DPR business license, not merely employ somebody certified, and each location keeps a Designated Certified Applicator on staff. Ask which category your technician holds.

Where else along the U.S. 78 corridor do we work?

Our address is Windsor, further east on the same highway. West on 78 the corridor runs into Aiken and the developments on its south side such as Cedar Creek; northeast, past the farm country, is Wagener. The full service-area list sits here, and you can describe the problem to us directly.

Frequently asked questions

Is Montmorenci a town?

No. It is an unincorporated community in Aiken County on U.S. Route 78, about 5.3 miles southeast of Aiken, at ZIP 29839 and 482 feet of elevation, with a post office. It is neither a chartered municipality nor a census-designated place, so no population figure is published for it.

There is no city code office out here. What can I do about a neighboring property?

We cannot advise you on that and will not pretend otherwise on a pest control page. Aiken County is the local government covering this area, and what it can address is a question to put to the county. What we do is work your side of the line, assuming the outside pressure is permanent.

Can you treat safely around a private well?

Yes, by leading with methods that involve no product near the casing. We seal the sanitary cap, clear stored material back from the well head, and rely on trapping and exclusion in that zone. Labels carry restrictions concerning wells and water, those directions bind the applicator, and we say plainly where we are not treating.

Do you treat inside a septic tank?

No, and nobody should. A septic tank is a working biological system, and pouring pesticide in damages the treatment while solving nothing. Roaches associated with a septic system get handled at the exits instead: a seated riser lid, an intact cleanout cap, sound vent piping, and water kept in every unused fixture trap.

Large roaches keep coming up the shower drain at night. What is that?

Almost always American cockroaches using a dry trap or an open cleanout as a route in from outside or from the septic system. One or two after dark near plumbing is a route problem, not an indoor breeding population. Run water through unused fixtures weekly and treat the exterior harborage instead.

I keep livestock, dogs and chickens. What will you actually use?

The program is built around those animals from the first visit. Canine detection involves no product at all. Rodent work opens with trapping and physical exclusion instead of bait, since a poisoned rodent stays available to whatever eats it. Any rodenticide goes into secured exterior stations, never near stored feed.

Do you handle termite inspections or a CL-100 letter for a closing?

Neither. We do not treat termites, write wood infestation reports or sell termite bonds, so a property sale needs a separate licensed firm for that document. We would rather tell you in the first minute of the call than book the appointment and hand you off in the yard.

h1: Pest Control in New Ellenton, SC

hero.eyebrow: NEW ELLENTON, SOUTH CAROLINA · PEST CONTROL
hero.h1: Pest Control in New Ellenton, SC
hero.lead: New Ellenton was chartered in 1952 to receive people evicted from Ellenton for the Savannah River Plant, and some of them brought their houses with them. Coastal K-9 & Pest Solutions handles ants, roaches, spiders, rodents and bed bugs here, and starts at the gaps rather than the spray can.
hero.meta: Call 803-226-3155 · Family-owned · Based at 320 Wendy Lane, Windsor, SC · Ten miles down SC 19 from Aiken · Aiken County and the wider CSRA
badges: K-9 bed bug and rodent detection

body:
Most towns grow. This one arrived. On 28 November 1950 the Atomic Energy Commission announced the plant that became the Savannah River Site, and five communities inside the construction boundary had to go. Ellenton’s deadline to be empty was 1 March 1952. New Ellenton was chartered seven weeks later, on a two-hundred-acre tract fourteen miles north.

We raise it for one practical reason. A pest inspection is largely an inspection of joints, and the joints here have an unusual origin. A house lifted onto a truck and set down on a new foundation is not assembled the way a house built in place is.

6,000People relocated for the Savannah River Plant land acquisition, at an estimated $19,000,000 for all property, land and utilities (SRS Heritage Museum)
5,984Graves moved from 126 of the 161 cemeteries inside the construction boundary; 35 stayed (SRS Heritage Museum)
42%COUNTY-level: share of Aiken County housing units over forty years old in 2023 (SRSCRO Aiken-Augusta Regional Housing Study, 11 September 2025, p. 14)

What does general pest control actually cover here?

  • Ants, both outdoor nests foraging indoors and colonies already inside
  • German and American cockroaches, two different problems sharing one word
  • Spiders and the occasional invaders behind them: silverfish, crickets, beetles
  • Rats and mice: detection, exclusion, trapping, and the carpentry that holds
  • Bed bugs, screened by a certified detection dog, handled apart from the rest
  • Sweeps, mesh, screens and sealed penetrations as the first line, not the last
  • Commercial programs for small business stock and multi-address owners

What we do not do belongs in the same breath. We are not a wood-destroying-organism company, we do not write inspection letters for a closing, and we run no lawn programs. If that is your need we say so. Everything above sits under general pest control.

Why is this town’s housing stock unlike anywhere else in the county?

Because a good deal of it did not originate here.

The record is clear on the outline and thin on detail. The Corps of Engineers relocated 126 of the 161 cemeteries inside the boundary, containing 5,984 graves. Roughly six thousand living people were moved. The Savannah River Site Heritage Museum records that residents often took the first offer and moved the house itself outside the line, and carries a 1951 photograph of one on the highway.

People here descend from those households and some remember it, so we will not be cute about it. The technical point is narrow: this town’s built fabric dates almost entirely from one short window at the start of the 1950s, and part of it is older buildings re-founded rather than constructed.

What is not documented anywhere we could find is how many buildings were moved, or their condition now. Anyone quoting you a number has guessed.

What does a moved house have that a built-in-place house does not?

Seams. A relocated structure gets a second birthday, and the joint between the old building and its new footing was never designed alongside the rest.

The sill-to-foundation line

Where a house is set down on new masonry, the contact between sill plate and wall top was made on site, from whatever was to hand. Seventy years on, that is where we find daylight: a mouse-sized opening running a whole wall.

Foundation infill and skirting

The original building had one footing profile and the new site another. The difference gets closed with block, brick, infill or skirting, and those weather at different rates. A Norway rat reads a failed mortar joint in a pier wall the way you read a doorway.

Re-run utilities

Water, drain, gas and power had to be brought in fresh. Penetrations cut after a building exists are rarely sealed to the standard of ones formed during construction, and the gap around a supply line suits rodents and roaches alike.

Porches, steps and additions

Anything that could not travel was rebuilt on arrival. A porch band joist scabbed onto an older wall leaves a void the width of the porch, no vapor barrier under it. We check that early.

Racked openings

Anything hauled over a road flexes. Frames that shifted a quarter inch and were shimmed back square leave voids behind the trim, connecting wall cavity to open air.

None of this makes a moved house a bad house. It means the inspection map is different, and a slab-on-grade checklist walks straight past the points that matter.

What does one narrow build window do to pest pressure?

It makes failure uniform, which cuts both ways.

A town platted and built across a few years has one generation of framing, one of crawl space venting, one of door hardware, one of pipe detailing. They reach the end of their service life together, which is why one street produces five similar callouts in a season.

We can give you county context and no town figure, because the town figure does not exist in citable form. Across Aiken County, 42 percent of housing units were over forty years old as of 2023 (SRSCRO, September 2025). That is a county number and we label it as one.

Pressure here is therefore structural, not behavioral. In a new subdivision, roaches are usually about what came in on a box. In stock of this age, about a gap. Our exclusion and repair work exists for this profile.

Does a vacant house next door make your house worse?

Yes, and the city is already acting on it. New Ellenton currently holds a Community Development Block Grant funding demolition of blighted buildings — a live, citable signal about the condition of part of the stock.

An empty building is not empty. No temperature control, no maintenance, nobody closing a door, often no intact glazing. It becomes a reservoir: rodents nest undisturbed, American cockroaches use the damp crawl space, and it carries a larger population than a lived-in house would.

Two things follow at the property line. First, range: a house mouse works a small territory, but a Norway rat travels a hundred feet and more to reach a bin, a pet dish or a fruit tree. Second, demolition evicts them. The day a blighted structure comes down, whatever lived in it needs the next roof, and the next roof is a neighbor’s.

If a building near you is coming down, have your exclusion looked at that week, not the month after the mice show up.

How do you keep rodents out of a 1950s house on sandy ground?

With measurements, not with product. The numbers are small and unforgiving.

  • A house mouse needs about a quarter inch. If a pencil fits, a mouse fits. That is the standard we hold a building to.
  • A rat needs about half an inch and will enlarge anything smaller. Rodent incisors grow continuously and cut soft mortar, foam and vinyl without effort.
  • Quarter-inch hardware cloth, not window screen. Insect screen over a crawl space vent buys one season. Galvanized quarter-inch mesh, cut oversize and fastened, is what lasts.
  • Copper mesh plus sealant at penetrations. Steel wool rusts through and foam alone is a chew toy. Mesh packed to fill the void, then sealed, gives the tooth nothing to work against.
  • Door sweeps, then the corners. A worn sweep leaves a wedge of daylight at each end of the threshold. On a garage door the failure is where the astragal meets the jamb.
  • The utility band. Water, power, gas and dryer vent enter within a few feet of each other, all cut oversize. On a relocated house every one was cut after the building existed. Treat the band as one job.
  • Sandhills soil changes the below-grade picture. This is the Aiken Plateau: sandy soils from fine sand to loam, minimal organic matter, rapid percolation, poorly drained pockets in the low ground. Loose sand is easy digging for a burrowing rat, and it lets backfill settle away from a pier, opening a void under a foundation that looked continuous.

Detection comes first. We run certified dogs to locate activity inside a structure rather than guess from droppings in one corner, and we say plainly that no field-validated accuracy figure exists for structural rodent detection; the published validation work is on bed bugs. Method on the rodent control page; detail in the house mouse and Norway rat profiles.

German or American cockroach — which one do you have?

Not two sizes of one problem. Different habitat, different route in, different ending.

German cockroach: indoors, and it was carried in

Small, tan, two dark stripes behind the head. It does not live outdoors in South Carolina in any meaningful way. It arrives in a grocery bag, a carton, a second-hand appliance or a moving load, then stays within a few feet of warmth, water and food: motor housings, cabinet hinges, the void behind a dishwasher. Spraying a foundation line outdoors does nothing to it. See the German cockroach profile.

American cockroach: outdoors, and it walked in

The big one, up to an inch and a half, reddish brown, the one people call a palmetto bug. It genuinely lives outside here — crawl spaces, mulch, leaf litter, drain and sewer lines, the damp under a porch. It enters by a floor drain, a dry trap, a crawl space hatch or a gap at a pipe. One in the bathtub at 2 a.m. is a plumbing story, not a housekeeping one. The American cockroach profile has the life cycle.

Why this town splits along that line: the crawl spaces and pier foundations here are American cockroach habitat, and the damp pockets between the sandy uplands keep them supplied through a dry summer. German pressure tracks turnover, not geography. Both are on our cockroach control page.

Why does a detection dog answer a different question than a flashlight?

A visual bed bug inspection finds evidence: fecal spotting, cast skins, the odd dead insect. Evidence is durable. A room treated two years ago still carries staining behind the headboard, and staining says something happened, not that something is happening. A properly imprinted dog is trained to the odor of live insects and viable eggs — a present-tense answer.

Speed is the second difference, and it changes what you can afford to check. A dog clears a bedroom in a couple of minutes without dismantling the bed, so screening every sleeping room becomes realistic. The quiet rooms hold the surprises.

The limits get said out loud. An alert means scent is present at that spot: it does not count insects, does not date an infestation, and degrades in a hot room or with a tired dog. Every alert gets visual confirmation, and where it stays ambiguous we leave interceptors and return. Our founder, Kimberly Camera, has twenty-eight-plus years in scent detection, including canine work for FEMA Urban Search & Rescue. Teams certify through NESDCA, WDDO, CPDA and ICRWDA. See the K-9 bed bug detection page and the bed bug profile.

Why does exclusion come before chemistry?

Because a pesticide has a service life and a sealed hole does not.

Reverse the order and here is what you buy: a treatment that knocks the population down, an entry route still open, and a re-infestation on a schedule the weather sets. How often that repeat visit comes is the economics of a pest contract, and the building sets it far more than the chemical does.

In the right order the material work happens once. Seal the utility band, mesh the vents, fit the sweeps, repair failed mortar and rotted trim, correct the drainage keeping a crawl space damp. Treatment then enters a building with fewer ways in than it had that morning.

Who has to be licensed before anyone treats your house?

Structural pest control here is licensed by the Clemson University Department of Pesticide Regulation — the land-grant university, not a state agriculture department, which catches nearly everyone out. The category is 7A, Industrial, Institutional, Structural and Health-Related Pest Control.

A legitimate firm holds a DPR business licence, keeps a Designated Certified Applicator at each location, and carries general liability cover of at least $100,000 combined single limit with no deductible above $1,000. Ask for those before anyone opens a can on your property.

What we cannot tell you about New Ellenton

Most statistics you would want for a town this size do not exist or are unfit to print. Here is the gap instead.

  • The population figure is contested. The 2020 Census count, certified by the Municipal Association of South Carolina, is 2,210. The American Community Survey five-year estimate says 2,837, some 28 percent higher. We use 2,210.
  • No town-level housing-age table exists. Median year built, year built by decade, tenure split and vacancy rate are not retrievable for this place from a citable source. That is why the 42 percent above is labelled county-level.
  • We verified no subdivision name here. Not one. The streets we can source come from municipal and school addresses: Main Street North and South, which is SC Highway 19, plus Pine Hill Avenue and South Boundary Avenue.
  • No count exists for the relocated houses. The move is thoroughly documented. The inventory is not.
  • No flood claim. We could not open the county’s environmental review volume, so we make no floodplain statement about any address.

The setting we can source. This is Sandhills country on the Aiken Plateau, the town is listed at 427 feet across 4.44 square miles, and it sits about a mile north of the Savannah River Site — a Department of Energy reservation of 310 square miles and 198,046 acres, largely undeveloped and forested.

Where else do we work around New Ellenton?

Our base is 320 Wendy Lane in Windsor. We cover Jackson, which lost part of its own footprint to the same 1950 boundary before the construction parameters shifted; Aiken, ten miles north up SC 19; Windsor to the east; and Montmorenci. The full list is on our service areas page.

Frequently asked questions

Does it matter whether my house was one of the moved ones?

It changes where we look first, not what we charge. On a relocated structure we start at the sill-to-foundation line, the foundation infill, and the penetrations cut after the building existed. On a house built in place, at the crawl space vents and thresholds.

A house near mine is being demolished. Should I do anything?

Yes, and beforehand. Vacant buildings hold larger rodent and roach populations than occupied ones because nothing disturbs them, and demolition puts all of it on the move in an afternoon. Neighboring houses absorb them. Have your exclusion checked before the work, not the month after.

Why is the same spray not working on my kitchen roaches?

Most likely because they are German cockroaches and the product repels. Repellent sprays scatter that species deeper into voids and adjacent rooms, and the population rebuilds from what you pushed out of reach. They respond to gel baiting, sanitation and harborage reduction, not perimeter spray.

Is a big roach in my bathtub a hygiene problem?

Usually not. That is almost always an American cockroach, which lives outdoors in crawl spaces, mulch and drain lines and comes in by a plumbing route or a gap. The fix is a dry trap refilled, a drain screened, a hatch sealed and the utility penetrations closed. Cleaning harder changes nothing.

How small a gap actually matters?

A quarter inch for a house mouse, about half an inch for a rat, and both enlarge an opening that starts smaller. A worn door sweep, a corroded crawl space vent, a gap at the dryer vent or a settled joint under a sill plate all qualify. We work to the quarter-inch standard throughout.

Can you screen a rental unit between tenants?

That is the ideal moment. An empty unit lets a detection dog work fast and lets us mesh, seal and fit sweeps without scheduling around anyone. For bed bugs it is the only point at which an owner can document a baseline before the next resident moves in.

Should I trust a dog rather than an inspector with a flashlight?

Use both, and we do. A dog is trained to live insects and viable eggs, so it answers whether something is active now; a visual inspection finds evidence that persists long after a treatment worked. We confirm every alert visually, and where the picture stays unclear we set interceptors and return.

Does living beside the Savannah River Site change anything?

For outdoor-origin pests, yes. The boundary sits about a mile south and the reservation runs to 310 square miles of largely undeveloped, forested land. That is a very large undisturbed edge for a town this size, and it raises pressure from what lives outside and comes in: American cockroaches, occasional invaders, rodents working a wooded margin.

hero.lead: Coastal K-9 & Pest Solutions handles ants, cockroaches, spiders, rodents and bed bugs for North Augusta households and businesses. This is a South Carolina address inside a metro that runs on both banks of the Savannah River, so we work it under South Carolina credentials and will tell you plainly what those credentials cover.

body:
Ask somebody here where they ate last night and there is a fair chance the answer is in another state. About 27,000 people live on twenty square miles of South Carolina land, and the bridges carry an enormous share of ordinary business — jobs, groceries, doctors, the airport, dinner — into Augusta, Georgia and back.

That is a pleasant way to live. It also complicates a pest problem three ways. Licensing, because the two states run separate systems and a firm advertising into both had better be right on both. Movement, because insects and rodents travel with people and freight. And choice, because you can hire from two states. General pest control is where all three land.

26,982Estimated residents, 1 July 2025 (US Census QuickFacts, table PST045224)
1,679Housing units vacant of 12,694 citywide (US Census, ACS 2023 5-year, table DP04)
$100,000Minimum general liability for a South Carolina structural firm, combined single limit (Clemson DPR)

What does general pest control cover on this side of the river?

The animals that come to you, rather than the ones you go looking for. Augusta is the fall-line city of the Savannah River, so this bank sits on the Fall Line and inside the Sandhills belt, on deep quartz sands of the Lakeland and Fuquay series. Rain drains through that ground rather than standing on it — 50.77 inches a year, a 64.1°F mean, 232 freeze-free days at AIKEN 4 NE. Warm seasons and fast sand favor ground-nesting ants and give outdoor roaches most of the calendar.

Ants

Odorous house ants trail in along plumbing and slab edges after heavy rain; imported fire ants own open sunlit turf. Baiting beats spraying, which removes foragers and leaves the queens.

Cockroaches

Two species, two entirely different jobs, compared below. A wrong identification is the commonest reason a homeowner pays twice. Cockroach control starts with the correct name.

Spiders

Largely a harborage question. Clear webbing at eaves and garage corners, keep boxes off concrete, reduce the insects they feed on. Black widows are genuinely present in sheds and meter boxes. Spider control is mostly exclusion.

Invaders and rodents

Silverfish, flies, wasps at soffits, and the mice and rats that follow food indoors. Sealing earns its keep, which is why our repair and exclusion crew outperforms anything on the truck.

Two things we do not hold ourselves out for: termite work of any kind, wood-infestation letters included, and mosquito programs.

Which state licenses the company knocking on your door?

Almost nobody here asks, and it has the clearest answer on this page. The two states license structural pest control through different bodies, and neither license reaches the other bank. South Carolina hands the job to a university, which catches out anyone assuming an agriculture department holds it. Georgia does use its agriculture department.

 Your North Augusta addressAn address across the bridge
RegulatorClemson University Department of Pesticide RegulationGeorgia Department of Agriculture, Structural Pest Division, with the Structural Pest Control Commission, under O.C.G.A. section 43-45
Category7A, Industrial, Institutional, Structural and Health-Related Pest ControlHousehold Pest Control, one of several operator categories
Firm credentialDPR business licenseStructural Pest Control Company License
Named individualA Designated Certified Applicator at each locationA Certified Operator, plus Registered Employee status for technicians
Insurance floorAt least $100,000 combined single limit, no deductible above $1,000Set by the Georgia commission, not the South Carolina rule

None of this is a knock on Augusta firms. Plenty are credentialed in both states, and South Carolina companies hold Georgia licenses for the same reason. The narrower point belongs to you: a truck wrap does not say which license covers your house, and asking is ordinary.

  • The South Carolina license number, which is the structural pest license from Clemson DPR, not a municipal one.
  • The Designated Certified Applicator for the location serving you, by name. South Carolina requires one per location, not one per company.
  • A certificate of insurance. The floor is $100,000 combined single limit with no deductible over $1,000, and it is routine to ask.
  • Both credentials, if you own on both banks. Many firms carry the pair; some find the gap at the second address.
  • What gets applied, where and at what rate, on a service ticket. The label is the law.

How does a metro split by a river move its pests around?

Efficiently, and mostly inside things people are carrying. Nearly every structural pest here is a hitchhiker, so the question is what it arrived in.

Bed bugs make the clearest case. No wings, no jumping legs, no crossing a parking lot unaided. They move in luggage, a mattress carried down a staircase, a recliner bought secondhand. The origin of a North Augusta bed bug problem is therefore very often not North Augusta — it is a hotel room, a rental or a relative’s spare room elsewhere in the metro, and a state line means nothing to it. German cockroaches do the same at smaller scale, riding in cardboard or a used microwave.

Two local features deserve naming as habitat rather than scare story, since no agency publishes pest counts here and we will not invent any. The first is the Greeneway. Thomas W. Greene was mayor from 1985 to 1997 and the trail carries his name; the city puts it at over seven miles of paved path on an abandoned railroad corridor, Pisgah Road at one end and, at the other, Riverside Boulevard by the River Golf Club, with a mile-and-a-half extension threading the Crystal Lake area down to the water. A continuous vegetated edge with dependable cover is a line wildlife follows — geometry, not a counted population.

The second is empty housing. Of 12,694 units, 1,679 stand vacant, and rental vacancy runs 12.6 percent against 2.3 percent for owner units. Nobody sweeps an empty unit or hears anything in it at 2am. Where it shares a wall with yours, it is not next door — it is part of your building.

Then the calendar. City-owned SRP Park opened on 12 April 2018, seats 4,782 and takes up to 10,000 for larger events, with the Augusta GreenJackets playing there. The 2026 Masters runs 9 to 12 April at Augusta National, in Georgia rather than here — but the beds those patrons sleep in are spread over both banks.

German or American cockroach — which one are you looking at?

Settle this before anyone quotes you. The two species live differently, arrive differently and fall to different methods; a program built for the wrong one fails on schedule.

 German cockroachAmerican cockroach
LookHalf an inch, tan, two dark lengthwise stripes behind the headAn inch and a half or more, reddish brown, a pale figure-of-eight marking
Where it livesIndoors only, feet from warmth, water and foodOutdoors by preference — sewers, meter vaults, mulch, crawl spaces
How it arrivesCarried in cardboard, appliances, grocery bags, secondhand furnitureWalks or flies in through drains, sump pits, door gaps, weep holes
What worksGel bait in harborage, vacuuming, growth regulator, sanitation, timeExclusion, drains and sumps, moisture correction, an exterior perimeter
What backfiresBaseboard aerosol — it repels, scatters the population and ruins baitInterior fogging, when the source is outside or in the plumbing

The practical test is location and behavior. One large roach crossing a bathroom floor after a storm is nearly always the American species arriving by drain or door gap; the answer is a sweep, a drain screen and a look underneath the house. A few small striped roaches near a coffee maker is the German species breeding indoors, and daylight sightings mean it is well past its early stage. Both sit in the library: the German cockroach and the American cockroach.

How small a gap does a rodent need, and what closes it?

Smaller than one you would notice walking past. A house mouse passes roughly a quarter of an inch, about six millimetres; a rat manages half an inch. Exclusion beats bait over any long horizon, because a sealed hole stays sealed while a bait station has to be right forever. We work outside in, since openings are rarely where the noise is.

  • Grade line and slab edge. Settlement cracks, gaps behind stoops, trench backfill over a water line that never consolidated.
  • Weep holes and garage corners. Weep holes must keep draining, so the fix is a stainless or copper insert sized to pass water and stop a mouse, never mortar. A garage door seal rides up at each end and leaves a triangular void; corner pads and an astragal close it.
  • Utility penetrations. Line sets, condensate drains, dryer vents, gas, cable, fibre, each cut by a different trade on a different day. Sheet metal at 22 to 24 gauge, mechanically fastened, then sealant. Sealant alone is only an air seal.
  • Vents, thresholds and mesh. Crawl space louvres corrode from the inside out; back them with quarter-inch hardware cloth. Thresholds want a quarter-inch gap at most and a sweep meeting the frame at both corners. Half-inch mesh against rats, quarter-inch against mice, woven rather than welded, since welded joints part under gnawing.

Where a rat digs rather than climbs, the dimensions are settled: a curtain wall three feet below grade, an L-footing returning about a foot outward, or a two-foot gravel band. Sandhills sand digs easily, so the barrier has to be built rather than sprayed. Trapping and follow-up sit under rodent control, species detail in the Norway rat profile; where sign is thin or the building occupied we bring a dog, which is K-9 rodent detection in North Augusta.

Why does a bed bug problem here usually begin somewhere else?

For the reasons above, and because this insect is unusually good at being carried and unusually bad at being seen early. Nobody spots six in a box spring seam. People notice at week ten.

That lag is why detection is a decision separate from treatment. A visual inspection gathers evidence — fecal spotting, cast skins, the odd carcass — and evidence lingers. Staining behind a headboard proves that something happened at some point, which is a different sentence from something is happening now. A properly imprinted dog is trained on the odor of live insects and viable eggs, so its answer is in the present tense, and it clears a bedroom in minutes without the bed coming apart.

A dog will not give you a count, a duration, or a species other than the one it was imprinted on, and every alert gets a visual check before it reaches a report. Kimberly Camera, who founded the company, has spent more than twenty-eight years working detection dogs, a run that includes FEMA Urban Search and Rescue deployment. Treatment is its own craft and we do it — see bed bug control — but the order matters: find it, prove it, price it, treat it, verify it. Screening runs under K-9 bed bug detection in North Augusta.

What should you check before you sign with anybody?

Two states of competitors means two states of advertising, and some claims do not survive contact with a source. Apply these to us as readily as to anyone.

  • An inspection before a price, then a written scope naming the pests included, the pests excluded, the visit count and what a callback costs.
  • Any percentage claim. Ask its source. Canine bed bug detection has published field research behind it; structural rodent detection by dog has nothing comparable, so we publish no accuracy figure for that service and read anyone else’s warily.
  • The fire statistic. A much-repeated line assigns rodents a large share of fires of unknown origin. We traced it to a state fact sheet citing nobody, with nothing from the NFPA or the US Fire Administration behind it. Gnawed wire is a real hazard; that number is not.
  • Brown recluse. If a firm says your house has them, ask on what basis. A statewide review found 44 verified specimens from six counties over the fifty-one years to 2004, against 738 physician diagnoses in 2004 alone.
  • Who performs the repair, and what arrives on paper. Months later, a dated record of what was found and applied is the only version anyone can check.

Which North Augusta businesses do we actually work in?

A claim we will not make, having checked and failed to support it: no warehouse, distribution center, food plant or manufacturer could be verified as physically inside this city. Regional employers get attached to North Augusta routinely and should not be. Kimberly-Clark operates at Beech Island, Bridgestone’s Aiken plant is at Graniteville, and Textron Specialized Vehicles is in Augusta, Georgia. The commercial story here is lodging, food service, offices, retail and apartments.

Lodging. January 2019 brought the Crowne Plaza to 1060 Center Street: 180 guest rooms and suites over five floors, plus 11,000 square feet of meeting space and a ballroom of 5,400. It is the one hotel we could confirm here by name, and no room-inventory total for the city is published, so we quote none. That shape needs a back-of-house program across kitchen, banquet storage, loading and refuse, plus turnover discipline for bed bugs — our hotels and hospitality program.

Food service. Riverside Village broke ground as Project Jackson in May 2017 by the 13th Street Bridge: roughly thirty to thirty-five acres of mixed use worth around $200 million, with restaurants, a brewery, an amphitheater, apartments and offices. SRP Park sits inside it, and stadium concessions run flat out for three hours then stand idle for days, a rhythm both roach species exploit. Know your inspector: since 1 July 2024, South Carolina retail food establishments have been scored by the Department of Agriculture rather than DHEC, on the hundred-point sheet in Regulation 61-25, where above 87 is an A. See restaurant and food service.

Offices, retail and apartments. Merovan Business Center, Interchange Business Park and Martintown Professional Office Park are on the plat record. In that kind of building a plenum and a bin enclosure are shared, so one tenant’s finding is seldom one tenant’s problem. Multifamily runs to about 2,475 units, roughly 19.5 percent of the stock, plus 1,182 attached townhouses.

What is not here. Ten schools serve the city, but there is no college campus and no purpose-built student housing: Aiken Technical College is at Graniteville, USC Aiken is in Aiken, and Augusta University, Augusta Tech and Paine are in Georgia. No hospital or senior-living community could be verified inside the limits either.

Does the Georgia Avenue and Butler Avenue district need different handling?

Yes, and it is worth being precise about how small it is. The National Register listed it on 5 April 1984 under reference 84002017: roughly thirty acres taking in Martintown Road and the Observatory, Butler and Georgia Avenues, on a hill looking across at Augusta. Sixteen properties are counted: thirteen buildings that contribute, three structures that do not, and a cemetery. Significance runs from roughly 1859 to roughly 1930, though 1903 to 1907 accounts for most of the construction. Star of Edgefield dates to 1859: red brick, with iron posts carrying a veranda on two levels. Palmetto Lodge, 1903, is Tudor Revival, its half-timbering set into a roof of several gables. On the ground that means deep original millwork, built-ins nobody can pull out to look behind, roof valleys in quantity, and outbuildings that turn one address into several.

Past that we stop: the nomination is a residential document, it describes none of Georgia Avenue’s storefronts, and no other source we found gives their build dates or construction type. One boundary note, because it confuses people every year — Butler Creek runs in Richmond County, Georgia, where the USGS gauges it, while Savannah Rapids Park belongs to Columbia County, Georgia, up at the headgates of the Augusta Canal. Butler Avenue and Butlers Mill are unrelated South Carolina names.

Where do we work in and around North Augusta?

Coastal K-9 & Pest Solutions · 320 Wendy Lane, Windsor, SC 29856 · 803-226-3155 · Kim@ck9ps.com. We are an Aiken County firm working an Aiken County city, the second largest in the county by its own reckoning.

Inside the limits we cover Martintown Road, the historic avenues, Knox Avenue and the Five Notch side, Hammond’s Ferry and Riverside Village, Crystal Lake, the Greeneway corridor, and a residential belt taking in Walnut Grove, Knollwood, Butlers Mill, Hammond Hills, Wando Woodlands, Pinehurst, The Rapids and The Summit. Beyond the city we work Beech Island, Jackson and Graniteville, and on into Aiken and its neighborhoods, Gregg Park among them; the full list is on our service areas page. Birds and waterfowl are separate: bird control in North Augusta and goose control in North Augusta.

Frequently asked questions

Does my pest company need a South Carolina license, or is a Georgia one acceptable?

South Carolina. At a South Carolina address the licensing authority for structural work is Clemson University’s Department of Pesticide Regulation, Category 7A. A Georgia Structural Pest Control Commission license authorizes Georgia work and stops at the river. Many firms hold both, which is proper. Ask which one covers your house rather than assuming.

An Augusta company advertises here constantly. Is there anything wrong with hiring them?

Not in the least, provided they hold the South Carolina credential for your address. Advertising crosses the bridge freely; licenses do not. Ask for the Clemson DPR business license number and the Designated Certified Applicator at the location servicing you. A well-run firm answers in a minute.

How do I tell which cockroach I have?

By size and by where you see it. Small, tan, half an inch, two dark stripes behind the head, clustered near a coffee maker means German cockroach and an indoor breeding population. Large, reddish brown, an inch and a half, crossing a floor alone at night means American cockroach coming from a drain or door gap. The treatments are not interchangeable.

Should I worry about brown recluse spiders?

Far less than the internet suggests. A statewide review found 44 verified brown recluse specimens from six South Carolina counties over the fifty-one years ending in 2004, against 738 physician-diagnosed bites in 2004 alone. Black widows are the species we do find, in meter boxes, sheds and stacked material.

We got home from a trip and something is biting. What first?

Do not spray, do not bag everything, and do not throw out the mattress yet. Consumer aerosols repel bed bugs and scatter them into wall voids and adjoining rooms, which makes the eventual job larger. Put the suitcase on a hard surface, leave the room alone, and have it screened. Bite marks alone are not diagnostic.

Do you handle termites or mosquitoes?

No. We are a general pest, cockroach, rodent and bed bug company with bird and goose work alongside it, and we do not offer termite treatment, wood-infestation reports or mosquito programs. Saying so at the first call saves a wasted appointment. Plenty of firms on either bank do that work daily, and one of them is who you want.

The house next door has been empty a year. Does that affect us?

It can, particularly in attached housing. Roughly one in eight housing units citywide stands vacant, and rental vacancy runs at 12.6 percent against 2.3 percent for owner units. An empty unit is unheated, unswept and unwatched, so activity there goes unnoticed until it reaches your side.

Can I see proof of license and insurance before you start?

Yes, and you should ask every firm you consider, ourselves included. You want the South Carolina structural pest license number, the Designated Certified Applicator named for the servicing location, and a liability certificate meeting the $100,000 combined single limit the state requires. Requesting all three is routine, not adversarial.

h1: Pest Control in Orangeburg, SC

hero.lead: Orangeburg is the only place we publish a page for where most households rent, and close to a third of its homes sit in buildings holding two, three or four units. Coastal K-9 & Pest Solutions works that building type for roaches, rodents and bed bugs, on scheduled route days out of Windsor.
hero.meta: Call 803-226-3155 · 320 Wendy Lane, Windsor, SC 29856 · Kim@ck9ps.com · Roughly 38 miles east in a straight line

body:
There is a building type almost nobody writes about, and Orangeburg is full of it. Not the detached house, not the managed complex with a leasing office. The duplex on a corner lot. The fourplex with four mailboxes on one post.

It is too small to carry a management company, too big for one household to control. It shares walls, a plumbing stack, usually an attic and often a crawl space, yet has no shared budget and nobody who can simply say yes. Everything below about pest control here follows from that.

55.4%Of occupied homes here are rented; owner occupancy is 44.6 percent per Census QuickFacts, ACS 2020–2024 five-year estimates. The surrounding county runs 67 percent owner-occupied
29.4%Of housing units sit in two-to-four-unit buildings: 12.1 percent two-unit, 17.3 percent three- and four-unit, ACS 2020–2024 five-year estimates
15.34 ftEdisto River crest downtown, 6–7 November 2024, past the 1928 and 2015 records by nearly a foot (National Weather Service, Columbia)

What does general pest control cover in a building like this?

The same as anywhere. What changes is the unit of work: the building, not the apartment.

  • Cockroaches — German in the kitchen, American in the crawl and drain line. See cockroach control.
  • Bed bugs — canine screening, treatment, then verification. See bed bug control.
  • Rodents — detection, trapping, and closing routes rather than restocking bait. See rat and mouse control.
  • Ants, spiders and the rest, plus exclusion: measured openings sealed in materials that last.

Not on the list: wood-destroying insect reports, CL-100 letters, fumigation, mosquito or lawn work.

Why is a duplex or a fourplex the hardest building in town to get treated?

Because of who is not in the room. A large property has an operating budget, a manager who signs, staff with keys. A house has an owner who decides. This has neither.

No shared budget. Work gets paid out of this month’s rent by whoever answers the phone. No reserve, no common-area contract, often nothing in writing between owners.

No single decision-maker. Each half of a duplex can carry its own deed and landlord, and the two may never have spoken. Even under one owner there are four leases and four answers to whether a stranger may come in Tuesday.

Access is the whole ballgame. Reaching three units out of four is not seventy-five percent of a treatment; the missed unit is the reservoir that refills the rest. Two local numbers sharpen that. Vacancy runs 22.5 percent, and an empty unit is the worst neighbor of all, because nobody reports anything from it. And 18.8 percent of residents moved in the previous year, so whoever knows when this began has often gone.

Where does a two-to-four-unit building actually connect?

Three, plus the shared utility closet where all three meet. A walk-through of one apartment sees none.

The plumbing stack

Kitchens and baths are stacked or backed against each other on purpose, so one waste line serves several units. Every point where a pipe passes a plate is a hole cut oversize by whoever was working that day.

The attic

One roof covers all of it. Whether the dividing wall runs up to the roof deck decides whether the attic is one space or four, and in a building this age the only honest way to know is to open the hatch and look.

The crawl space

Often one continuous space under the whole footprint, one vent line, one moisture regime. A failing trap under one kitchen wets the ground beneath somebody else’s floor.

Just under half the city’s housing went up between 1940 and 1970, median build year 1968. Sixty years of small trades work leaves holes that were somebody’s solved problem and nobody’s sealed hole.

What can one owner fix alone, and what needs the owner next door?

This is the part competitors leave out, because it does not close a sale. Some of this job is yours. Some is not, and no product changes it.

Inside your own controlNeeds the other owner or tenant
Sealing penetrations in your unit: under the sink, behind the range, at the stack collar.Sealing the shared attic or crawl, where work crosses a boundary that exists on paper, not in the structure.
Gel bait placed properly in your kitchen and left alone.The same in every kitchen in the same week, which is what ends it.
Fixing your leak, your dripping trap, your damp cabinet base.The leak behind a wall you each own half of.
Encasing a mattress and keeping it on.Screening either side before anyone calls yours clear.
Monitoring: traps, interceptors, dated counts.The decision to stop, which cannot come from one clear unit beside three untested.

What works. Be the owner who organizes it: a written request, a date, a figure covering the whole structure, an offer to split by unit count. The other owner is rarely hostile, just unaware the problem is theirs.

None of what follows is legal advice; we sell pest work, not opinions on your deed. Broadly, owner-and-tenant obligations sit in the lease and in whatever property maintenance code the jurisdiction adopted, while obligations between owners sit in the deeds. Take those to your own attorney. What we supply is the written finding these talks usually lack.

Why is the German cockroach a building problem and not a housekeeping problem?

Because nobody’s yard produces them. The species lives indoors permanently, arrives carried in, and persists in the warm, tight places a building offers. Sanitation is a real risk factor — an apartment rated poor for it is roughly three times likelier to be infested — but a spotless kitchen sharing a void and a waste line with one that is not will still have roaches.

So tenants buy cans: a HUD-funded UF/IFAS survey of 926 renters across 44 states found 79 percent self-treating. What the cans do is documented. A trial across five apartment complexes in BMC Public Health found foggers achieved no significant population reduction, having put as much as 603 times the baseline insecticide load onto counters and floors. Its companion paper found 96 percent of apartment-collected roaches carrying the kdr resistance mutation. The pyrethroid can under a tenant’s sink is, for that population, close to water. See the German cockroach profile.

How do rodents use a building with four front doors?

They ignore the doors. A rodent lives in the geography between units: a joist bay, a stud cavity, the run beside a waste line, the space above one ceiling and below another floor. It feeds where food is easiest and harbors where it is quietest, rarely the same apartment. One bait station outside one door is theatre. That tenant stops calling; the animal keeps a route crossing three leases.

  • Sizes are not a judgment call. A mouse passes an opening the size of a dime; a rat gets under a half-inch door gap.
  • Crawl vents have a published standard. The residential code requires under-floor ventilation coverings whose least dimension does not exceed a quarter inch. Torn screen on a 1960s vent fails on sight.
  • Gnawing decides the material. Foam and tape are placeholders; metal and mortar are closures.

See the Norway rat profile for what happens under a raised floor.

What does a canine screen settle when four units must be cleared at once?

Two things a flashlight cannot: how much of the building is involved, and whether you can stop. Worth knowing first — three of four strains in one study avoided deltamethrin-treated harborages, so spraying at the bed pushes survivors next door.

Coverage. In a published apartment study, brief visual inspection found 72 plus or minus 3 percent of the infestations present; interceptors left down over time found 89 plus or minus 1 percent. Roughly one infested unit in four reads clean to a quick look.

Time. In the best-documented multifamily program in the literature, initial inspection averaged 102 minutes per apartment. Four units done properly by eye is most of a day before anyone treats anything. A dog covers a room in minutes, which is what makes screening all four affordable.

Its elimination standard was three consecutive clean checks over 42 days, so budget for the verification period. See the bed bug profile and our multifamily program.

What did the November 2024 crest leave behind?

Orangeburg sits on the north fork of the Edisto, the only town in this part of our area with a documented flood of record. On 6 and 7 November 2024 the river crested at 15.34 feet downtown, past the 1928 and 2015 marks by nearly a foot. Roughly 35 roads closed and the low ground near Edisto Memorial Gardens was inundated.

Moisture outlasts the water. A street drains in hours; a crawl space does not. Ground, insulation and subfloor stay wet for weeks, and damp turns an occasional invader into a resident population. An ownership problem again: one owner’s wet ground sits under the neighbor’s joists.

Displacement moves things between buildings. When people leave with what they can carry and come back weeks later, bedding passes through other buildings on the way. That is how bed bugs and German cockroaches change addresses. Screen before the furniture goes back in. And no, a flood is not our cue to sell a moisture inspection.

Which agency licenses the company you let into a tenant’s kitchen?

Not a health department, and not the agriculture department. Licensing runs through Clemson University — its Department of Pesticide Regulation — the last door anybody thinks to knock on when checking a contractor.

  • Category 7A is the relevant one: industrial, institutional, structural and health-related work. Roaches, rodents and bed bugs sit inside it.
  • The company must hold a DPR business license. Employing somebody certified is not the same.
  • A Designated Certified Applicator is assigned to the location serving you, with liability coverage of at least $100,000.
  • Technicians complete DPR Verifiable Technician Training and are retrained annually.

That matters more when a company is not local, not less. Ask for the license number and applicator’s name before the appointment.

How do we actually serve a city this far out?

Plainly: this is the farthest point we publish a page for, and we will not pretend otherwise. Our shop at 320 Wendy Lane in Windsor is roughly 38 miles west in a straight line, further by road. Orangeburg does not face our direction anyway — it faces Columbia, about 37 miles northwest, and the I-26 corridor. The link from our end runs southeast on US 78 through Blackville, Denmark, Bamberg and Branchville.

So we run this city as scheduled route work on set days, grouped with other calls along that corridor. Whole-building screening fits: planned, everyone lined up anyway, valued for scope rather than speed. What we cannot offer is a truck at your door within the hour. If that is today’s problem, call a company in town.

From our end we also cover Williston, Salley and Wagener; the full list is on the service areas page. Two deliberate absences: no apartment property is named here, and we claim no flood zone for any address, since that comes off a FEMA panel for your parcel.

Rental demand here is explained by Claflin University, founded 1869 and the state’s oldest historically Black college; by South Carolina State, founded 1896 on the roots of an 1872 land-grant institute; and by manufacturing and a regional hospital. The building type explains the work.

Frequently asked questions

I own one half of a duplex. Can my half be treated alone?

It can, and we will do it. Whether it stays treated is another question. Roaches, mice and bed bugs move through the shared stack, void or attic, so a single-side job usually buys a quiet spell, not an end. We say which beforehand.

My tenant says the roaches came with the building. Possible?

Often, yes. German cockroaches do not live outdoors here, so they were carried in at some point and persisted. A unit can change hands already populated, with nothing visible at the walk-through. That is why we inspect first.

Do you insist on treating the whole building?

No, but we price it and explain the difference. Our preference is every kitchen baited in one week and every unit screened, because that is what the evidence supports. If one owner acts alone, we say in writing what that costs.

How fast can you get to Orangeburg?

Not same-day. We are roughly 38 miles off in a straight line and run this area on booked route days along the US 78 corridor. Planned jobs suit us and suit the building type; an emergency within the hour does not.

Who pays for treatment in a rented duplex?

Out of the lease and any adopted property maintenance code, not out of anything we can tell you. South Carolina has no bed-bug-specific statute, and habitability duties do not settle cost. Read the lease, then ask your own attorney.

Can you do a termite inspection or a CL-100 for my closing?

No. Our work is household pests, cockroaches, rodent detection with trapping and exclusion, and canine bed bug detection with treatment. Wood-destroying insect reports, moisture letters, fumigation and mosquito routes sit outside it. A referral serves you better.

Give us the unit count, who owns what, and whether there is a crawl space, an attic hatch or both. We will scope the screen to the structure, price it to be split, and report on every unit.

h1: Pest Control in Salley, SC

hero.lead: Salley holds 329 people in three-quarters of a square mile, and 99 of its buildings are National Register contributing structures. Coastal K-9 & Pest Solutions works this town for ants, spiders, cockroaches, rodents and bed bugs, and closes old buildings up without costing you the fabric you are trying to keep.
hero.meta: Call 803-226-3155 · Family-owned · Based in Windsor, SC · Eastern Aiken County, ZIP 29137

body:
In most towns the historic district is a few blocks you drive past. In Salley it is very nearly the town: listed on the National Register on 27 October 2000 with 99 contributing structures against 51 non-contributing, inside a boundary of four streets — Pine, Ferguson, Poplar and Aldrich.

So the question here is rarely which product to spray, but what you may do to a building while you shut it.

99Contributing structures in the Salley Historic District, National Register listed 27 October 2000 (SCDAH reference S10817702032)
0.77 sq miTotal area of the town, about 1.41 percent of it water
329Residents at the 2020 Decennial Census, certified in the Municipal Association of South Carolina record

Why is sealing a protected building a different job?

Because the quick fix and the correct fix are not the same thing, and here the quick fix is permanent damage. Ordinary exclusion is blunt. Foam the gap. Face-screw a galvanized plate over the vent. On a 1990s ranch nobody minds. Do it to an 1888 frame house or a 1906 bank front and you have made a change still visible in fifty years, applied with a gun, by somebody thinking about a mouse. Three rules apply instead.

  • Reversible. Every barrier comes back off with a screwdriver, leaving what was under it intact. Mechanical fasteners, not adhesive, reusing an existing hole where one exists.
  • Sympathetic. Anything that will be seen gets painted out or set back in the reveal. Bright new metal on a weathered elevation is an alteration whether or not anyone approved it.
  • Off the original fabric. We do not enlarge an opening to make a patch easier, rout a sill to seat a plate, or fasten into hand-planed siding when a later addition holds the same screw.

In practice that means working the unseen side. A foundation vent is screened from inside the crawl space, behind the original grille, so the grille is untouched and the mesh invisible from the yard. Masonry is addressed in the mortar joint, never the brick.

One clarification, since it gets muddled. Register listing does not by itself dictate what a private owner may do to their own house; it records that the building matters. We hold to these rules anyway. See exclusion and repairs.

How much of Salley is old building?

Most of it. Ninety-nine contributing against fifty-one non-contributing puts roughly two of every three buildings inside the boundary in the period the listing describes: a rural South Carolina community of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. The town was established on 19 December 1887 and grew as a shipping point for the farms around it, which is why Town Hall still sits on Railroad Avenue N.

Victorian and Bungalow architecture is named among its buildings, several individually: the Riley-Sawyer-Salley House of 1888, the Bank of Salley of 1906, a Coca-Cola warehouse from 1924, and the Salley High School Auditorium of 1936–1937, now the civic center.

As a pest inventory it reads: original framing and foundations still carrying load, wood siding as the weather line, additions layered across five decades of carpentry, outbuildings older than most people’s houses. The masonry commercial buildings are a separate job, which our commercial programs cover.

Salley was known statewide for the Chitlin’ Strut, which began in 1966 to pay for Christmas decorations and ran the Saturday after Thanksgiving. The town has cancelled the 2025 and 2026 events.

What is included in general pest control here?

Our household program, with nothing implied that we do not sell.

  • Ants — identified first, because odorous house, fire and carpenter ants each want a different answer.
  • Cockroaches — two separate programs, for reasons below. See cockroach control.
  • Spiders and occasional invaders — silverfish, camel crickets, millipedes, arriving from underneath rather than through a door.
  • Rodents — located, trapped, locked out. See K-9 rodent detection and rat and mouse control.
  • Bed bugs — canine screening and treatment. See bed bug control.
  • Exclusion carpentry — to a written specification, on the terms above.

Not sold and not implied: termite treatment, wood infestation reports, fumigation, lawn work, mosquito programs.

How do rodents get through original framing and outbuildings?

Through what a century and a third of movement has opened, and every hole drilled for a service the building was not built with. The dimensions are small and not negotiable. A house mouse gets through a quarter of an inch; a rat wants about half an inch. Both are smaller than gaps we routinely measure at a settled sill of this age, and neither animal hunts for the one bad spot — it works the line until the line gives. Our house mouse profile covers why two traps under a sink are theater.

  • Sill and foundation seat — where framing has dropped a fraction onto masonry, daylight runs the length of a wall instead of sitting in one hole.
  • Crawl space hatch — a wooden door on soil, rotted at a corner, held shut by a brick.
  • Later service penetrations — water, waste, gas, electric, cable, a heat pump line set drilled last and packed with foam. Six trades, six holes.
  • Original foundation vents — cast or wood grilles corroded or split. Screen behind them, never over them.
  • Outbuildings — sheds, smokehouses and detached garages, where a population builds unnoticed for a year.
  • Barn and shed doors — the gap under a sagging door is nearly always past half an inch. That is a rat door with a latch.

Specification separates a repair from a patch. Woven hardware cloth at half-inch mesh in 19 gauge holds rats; quarter-inch mesh in 24 gauge holds mice. Sheet metal barriers start at 24 gauge. Copper mesh is packing behind a hard cap, never the cap itself.

Two cockroaches, two separate problems

The one that lives under the house

American cockroaches are the large reddish insects people call palmetto bugs. They are outdoor animals — crawl space, mulch, sewer line, damp ground under a shed. In a raised turn-of-the-century house they climb plumbing chases and appear indoors singly, usually after rain. Three in a fortnight near a bathroom is a report about the space under the floor. American cockroach profile.

The one that arrives in a box

German cockroaches never walk in from a yard in this climate. They are carried in, then settle into warm harborage near food and water: dead space behind an old cabinet run, the void under a countertop set against plaster. Females hold the egg case almost to hatching, so treatment that misses harborage only delays them. German cockroach profile.

Chase the wrong one and you lose a season: a kitchen baited while the crawl space keeps sending replacements, or a crawl space treated while the colony sits twenty feet away behind a cabinet.

Do bed bugs turn up in a town of 329 people?

Yes, and town size has nothing to do with it. They travel on people and what people carry: a hospital stay, a hotel two hundred miles off, a secondhand recliner.

A visual inspection answers something narrow: whether a person can see evidence where a person can reach. Fair enough in a heavy infestation. Close to worthless early, and worse in a room treated once already, because a knocked-down population that was never eliminated hides better than a fresh one.

A canine screen answers a different question: whether live odor is present, including inside voids nobody can open, and which rooms are clear. In this housing stock the void count is the whole issue — plaster cracked at a settled corner, baseboard standing off the wall, plank floor seams, the joint where original trim meets an addition. What we will and will not claim from the research is on our canine detection accuracy page. Every indication is confirmed by hand, and a room the dog leaves alone is one you stop paying to treat.

What bait costs you in a wall you cannot open

Rodenticide is not illegitimate, and licensed applicators use it properly every day. It is simply the wrong opening move here, for a reason specific to the buildings: a poisoned rodent does not die where the bait sits. It dies wherever it happens to be — inside a stud bay behind lath and plaster, above a beadboard ceiling, in the floor structure over a crawl space. Getting it out means opening original material, in a hurry, in the middle of two weeks of odor, on a wall nothing had damaged until the bait went down.

Trapping returns a body, a location and a count: where the runway is, how large the population is, and when it has stopped. Order matters more than product choice — clear the interior, confirm quiet, then seal. Rodenticide belongs outside, in secured tamper-resistant stations, numbered and mapped.

What the data cannot tell you about a place this size

Population. The 2020 Census counted 329 residents; the American Community Survey five-year estimate says 288, twelve percent below that. The decennial number is the one we quote, since a head count beats a model drawn from a tiny sample.

Home value and poverty. Both exist for Salley and neither is usable. The median home value estimate carries an error band running to roughly ninety percent of the number itself, and the poverty figure is barely better. Neither is evidence of anything.

Housing age and subdivisions. No citable median year built exists for Salley and we will not model one; the count of 99 contributing structures is better evidence anyway. No subdivision name could be verified, so this page names none.

Who regulates this work in South Carolina?

Licensing sits with the Clemson University Department of Pesticide Regulation — not an agriculture department, which is why people checking credentials look in the wrong place. Structural work is Category 7A.

  • The firm holds its own DPR business license. Employing a certified person is not the same thing.
  • A Designated Certified Applicator must be on staff at the location serving you.
  • Holding the license requires general liability coverage of $100,000 or more.
  • Ask for the license number and category. Hesitation is an answer.

Kimberly Camera founded this company after twenty-eight-plus years in scent detection, certified through NESDCA, WDDO, CPDA and ICRWDA.

Coastal K-9 & Pest Solutions · 320 Wendy Lane, Windsor, SC 29856 · 803-226-3155 · Kim@ck9ps.com

Salley sits at the eastern edge of Aiken County, in Edisto-basin farm country. Our nearest stop is Wagener, minutes up the road, which holds all three schools this end of the county uses. West is Windsor, where the trucks and the dogs are kept, and past it Aiken. See every area we serve, or describe what you are finding.

Frequently asked questions

My house is in the historic district. Will your exclusion work alter it?

That is the constraint we design around. Barriers are mechanically fastened so they lift back off later, set behind original features rather than over them, and fixed into added material where one exists. Anything that would touch a visible feature gets discussed and photographed first, never decided on the ladder.

Can you use expanding foam? It is what the last company used.

Not on original woodwork. Foam stops air and nothing with teeth, so it fails at the job, and it bonds hard to old paint and soft wood, lifting fibers when it comes off. We use hardware cloth, sheet metal and sized backers instead.

The shed out back is older than the house. Is it worth treating?

It is usually where the work is. Outbuildings this age stay dry, unheated and undisturbed, which is ideal rodent harborage, and stored feed carries a population through winter. Treating the house while the shed keeps producing animals moves the problem rather than ending it.

Why not just set out bait boxes and be done?

Because a poisoned rodent dies inside your walls. In a plaster-and-lath house that means opening original material to reach an odor you will smell for a fortnight. Trapping gives us a body and a count, and tells us when a population has actually stopped.

How do I tell whether the roaches I am seeing are the serious kind?

Size and behavior. Big, reddish, an inch and a half, alone near a drain after rain: American, commuting up from under the floor. Half an inch, tan, two dark stripes behind the head, several at once by a refrigerator: German, which needs a real program rather than a spray.

Do you write CL-100 letters or handle termites?

No to both, and no to fumigation, lawn treatment or mosquito programs. Our list is household pest control, cockroach programs, rodent detection with exclusion, and bed bug detection with treatment. A closing that needs a wood infestation report needs another company.
